draft.title: Science changes with new evidence
card: A scientific idea, such as a model or a theory, is the best explanation that fits the evidence we have now. It is not fixed forever.
Better tools or new observations can turn up facts the old idea cannot explain. Scientists then change the idea or replace it.
Old evidence can also be looked at in a new way. A fresh explanation may fit that same evidence better.
For example, people once thought the Sun and planets moved around a still Earth. Telescope observations of moons circling Jupiter and of the phases of Venus fitted a Sun-centred model better.
draft.remember: Scientific ideas are revised when new evidence appears or old evidence is explained in a better way.

a.q: Why do scientists sometimes change a well-known model?
opts: New evidence does not fit the old model
The old model was never based on evidence
A new scientist always disagrees with it
The old model is too old to be useful
a.why: Models are kept because they fit the evidence. When new evidence does not fit, the model is revised. Age alone is not a reason, and the old model was built on the evidence available then.
a.clue: Think about what a model is meant to fit.

b.q: For years, a team in Geelong explained why a lake's fish numbers fell using the idea that warm weather was the cause. New water tests then showed a chemical in the lake that matched the drops in fish numbers. What should the team do with its idea?
opts: Revise it to take the new test results into account
Keep it, because it was the first explanation
Drop all earlier data, because it is now worthless
Ignore the tests, because the idea was well known
b.why: A scientific idea is the best fit to the evidence so far. The new tests are evidence the old idea may not explain, so the team should revise it. The earlier data is not worthless, since it can be re-read alongside the new results.
b.clue: What should happen when new evidence turns up?

a.best: New evidence does not fit the old model

b.best: Revise it to take the new test results into account
